summary.text: Divya Pidi is standing for Kororoit at the 2026 Victorian election, and the ABC's guide gives the party as The Republican. The ABC lists no website or biography for the candidate, and we found no party or campaign page as at early November 2026.

sources.title: Kororoit: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Donna Southern is The West Party's candidate for Kororoit at the 2026 Victorian election. She holds a PhD in health services research and has worked at the University of Melbourne and the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners. A third-generation resident of the western suburbs, she led a local push for traffic lights where Leakes Road meets the Western Freeway.

priorities.text: The West has been overlooked for way too long
Investment in basic local infrastructure such as roads, traffic lights, street lighting and pedestrian crossings
Help for families struggling with rising living costs

sources.title: Kororoit: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Donna Southern, The West Party for Kororoit

summary.text: Jack Chakoma is the Liberal candidate for Kororoit at the 2026 Victorian election. He came to Australia as a child and lives in Truganina. His work has involved supporting people affected by family violence and insecure housing, and the ABC says he once ran an agency that supported Australians from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

occupation.text: Support work for people affected by family violence and housing insecurity

prior_roles.organisation: Support agency for culturally and linguistically diverse Australians

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of living for households and businesses
More police and protective services officers back at train stations
Tougher sentencing laws

sources.title: Kororoit: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Jack Chakoma, Liberal for Kororoit, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Joyce McDonald is the Greens candidate for Kororoit at the 2026 Victorian election. She describes herself as a young trans woman from the local area. Her party page focuses on the cost of living, and the party had published no other biography as at early November 2026.

priorities.text: Ending the cost-of-living crisis for local families
a campaign in Kororoit that centres the community, inclusivity, compassion and social justice

summary.text: Luba Grigorovitch has been Labor's member for Kororoit since the 2022 election. Since April 2026 she has been Minister for Youth and Minister for Carers and Volunteers, after a period as Parliamentary Secretary for Outdoor Recreation. She previously led the Victorian branch of the Rail, Tram and Bus Union and served on Hobsons Bay council. She is recontesting Kororoit in 2026.

occupation.text: Trade union official (Rail, Tram and Bus Union)

summary.text: Nick Patterson is the Family First candidate for Kororoit at the 2026 Victorian election. His party page describes him as a Christian, married with five children, who has spent more than 20 years in Christian ministry and was a professional mixed martial arts fighter ranked first in Australia in two weight divisions. It says he ran a martial arts gym for 12 years until the COVID lockdowns forced it to close, after which he organised and spoke at freedom rallies.

occupation.text: Businessman and former professional MMA fighter

prior_roles.role: Owner and operator of a martial arts gym
prior_roles.note: The party page says he ran it for 12 years and that it closed during the COVID lockdowns.

priorities.text: Resisting government overreach and protecting individual liberty
Holding governments and police to account
Christian faith, strong families and personal responsibility

summary.text: Rayan Hassan is standing for the Victorian Socialists in Kororoit at the 2026 Victorian election. A youth worker who has studied and worked in Melbourne's west, he is a member of the Australian Services Union. He has been active in the Palestine solidarity movement and in refugee and anti-racism campaigns.

priorities.text: I stand for international solidarity, for refugee rights
Easing rent and mortgage pressure on working people in the west
Relieving overstretched schools and hospitals and fixing poor infrastructure

sources.title: Kororoit: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Seva Melnikov is One Nation's candidate for Kororoit at the 2026 Victorian election. He was born in Ukraine during the Soviet era and moved to Australia aged six. After studying psychology and philosophy at Monash University he worked at NAB, and he now works in cybersecurity.

sources.title: Kororoit: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Vasundhara Kandpal is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Kororoit at the 2026 Victorian election. Originally from the Himalayas, she has spent more than ten years in research, community education and social welfare work, largely in Melbourne's west. The party says she has set up women's sporting groups and run education programs for young families in Wyndham and Melton.

occupation.text: Research, community education and social welfare work

priorities.text: Ending cruelty in greyhound and horse racing in the west
Preventing crime, including break-ins, street and family violence and racist attacks
A safe, respectful community for people of every background and faith

sources.title: Kororoit: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Vasundhara Kandpal for Kororoit, Animal Justice Party Victoria
